categories.label: OAuth 2.0
categories.description: OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow with stateless JWT access + refresh tokens.

endpoints.title: Send the user to the install URL
endpoints.summary: Start the OAuth authorization code flow.
endpoints.description: This is a **dashboard** URL (https://{{dashboard}}, or the white-label dashboard host), not an API-host endpoint — you redirect the user's browser here. They see a consent page listing the scopes your app requests. If they are not logged in, myCRMSIM redirects them to the login page first and returns them here after sign-in. When they click Install, the browser is redirected to your redirect_uri with a single-use `?code=` query parameter, plus `state` echoed verbatim when you sent one. If they click Cancel, the browser is redirected to your redirect_uri with `?error=access_denied` (and the same `state`) and no code is issued.

params.name: client_id
params.description: The public client_id of your app (issued when your app is registered).

params.name: redirect_uri
params.description: Where myCRMSIM should send the user after consent. Must match the redirect_uri registered on the app.

params.name: state
params.description: Opaque value generated by your app (CSRF token). It is not interpreted by myCRMSIM and is returned unchanged, URL-encoded, as `state` on both the success and the cancel redirect. Verify it on your callback before exchanging the code.

endpoints.title: Exchange code for tokens
endpoints.summary: Exchange an authorization code for an access token and refresh token.
endpoints.description: Server-to-server. Send the code your callback received along with your client_id + client_secret. Returns both tokens — store them in your database, keyed by the installing user. Codes are single-use and expire 10 minutes after consent: a second exchange with the same code returns an error indicating that the code has already been used. If the exchange times out or returns a 5xx, retry it once; if the retry reports the code as already used, the first attempt was processed and no tokens can be recovered — send the user through the install URL again. The token endpoints are not covered by the per-installation API rate limits and do not return 429.

endpoints.title: Refresh tokens
endpoints.summary: Use the refresh token to obtain a new access token.
endpoints.description: When you get a 401 from the API ("Invalid or expired access token"), call this endpoint with your stored refresh_token to get a fresh pair. Replace both stored tokens with the new values. Access tokens expire after 24 hours (`expires_in`); refresh tokens after 1 year. Every refresh returns a new refresh token, but tokens are stateless signed JWTs: the previous refresh token is NOT invalidated by rotation and stays usable until its own expiry or until the installation is suspended. Keep only the newest pair. Because the old token stays valid, a refresh that times out or returns a 5xx is safe to retry with exponential backoff (for example 1 s, 2 s, 4 s). The token endpoints are not covered by the per-installation API rate limits and do not return 429.

categories.description: Sub-accounts / locations. Either a connected platform location or a stand-alone Custom Location.

endpoints.title: List workspaces
endpoints.summary: List workspaces (sub-accounts / locations) owned by the installer.
endpoints.description:
Returns the sub-account workspaces owned by the authenticated installer. The top-level "Company" account is excluded — only actual workspaces (Location / Custom Location, etc.) are returned. Each carries its `user_type`; server-side filtering by `user_type` is not supported, so clients filter client-side when needed.

**Pagination:** `limit` is clamped to [1, 200] (default 50) and `page` to >= 1 (default 1). To read past the first `limit` rows, request `page=2`, `page=3`, … until `page` reaches `total_pages`. Invalid bounds are normalised rather than rejected, and the response `pagination` object reports the applied `page` and `limit`, `total_pages`, the `max_limit` (200), the raw `requested_page` / `requested_limit`, and a `normalized` flag that is true when clamping changed a requested value.

**Ids:** `id` is the numeric workspace id used by every `/workspaces/{id}` path and `workspace_id` field. `remote_id` is the external platform location id (the `location_id` in the support articles) for Location workspaces, or a server-generated hex string for Custom Location workspaces.

params.name: limit
params.description: Page size — integer clamped to [1, 200]; default 50. Out-of-range or non-numeric values (0, negative, > 200, non-numeric) are normalised, NOT rejected; the applied bounds are echoed in the response `pagination` object (`limit`, `max_limit`, `requested_limit`, `normalized`).

params.name: page
params.description: 1-based page number; default 1. Clamped to >= 1 (page=0 becomes 1 and sets `normalized`). Rows are ordered by id descending, so with `limit` 200 and `total` 450 pages 1–3 return the full set. The applied page is echoed in `pagination.page`, with `total_pages` and the raw `requested_page`.

endpoints.title: Get workspace
endpoints.summary: Fetch a single workspace by id.
endpoints.description: Returns the workspace. When an inbound webhook is configured for the workspace, the response also includes an `inbound_webhook` object with the registered `url` and `headers`. When no webhook is configured, the field is omitted.

endpoints.title: Create workspace
endpoints.summary: Create a new Custom Location workspace.
endpoints.description:
Creates a stand-alone Custom Location workspace. The `remote_id` is generated server-side (a 20-character hex string) and is never accepted in the request body. A new workspace may take a few seconds to become fully active — if a follow-up call returns 404 immediately after creation, retry shortly.

Optionally pass `inbound_webhook_url` (and `inbound_webhook_headers`) to register an inbound webhook in the same call. When supplied, the webhook is registered on the workspace so inbound messages can be POSTed straight in. The webhook URL must be an `http(s)` URL.

params.name: email
params.description: Normalized to lowercase. Stored in meta.email.

params.name: url
params.description: Public website URL. Stored in meta.url.

params.name: inbound_webhook_url
params.description: Optional. When supplied, an inbound webhook row is created for this workspace so inbound messages can be POSTed to this URL. Must be http(s).

params.name: inbound_webhook_headers
params.description: Optional. Extra headers to forward with each inbound webhook delivery — typically an auth header. Sent as an array of `{ key, value }` objects, e.g. `[{ "key": "x-webhook-secret", "value": "abc123" }]`. Each entry must include a non-empty `key`.

endpoints.title: Update workspace
endpoints.summary: Partially update a workspace.
endpoints.description:
Send any subset of the writable fields. `remote_id` is not updatable — it ties the workspace to its source system, and changing it would break synchronization.

The inbound webhook can also be managed through this endpoint:
• Send `inbound_webhook_url` with a new URL to register or change the webhook (creates it if it does not yet exist).
• Send `inbound_webhook_headers` to update the headers — when omitted the previously stored headers are preserved.
• Send `inbound_webhook_url: ""` (or `null`) to remove the webhook entirely.

The response always includes the current `inbound_webhook` object when one is configured, mirroring **Get workspace**.

params.name: user_type
params.description: Must be "Custom Location" (the only workspace type the external API can manage).

params.name: inbound_webhook_url
params.description: Register, change, or clear the inbound webhook URL. Pass `""` or `null` to remove the webhook entirely. Must be http(s) when supplied.

params.name: inbound_webhook_headers
params.description: Replace the stored headers with this list. Sent as `[{ "key": "...", "value": "..." }]`. Omit to keep the existing headers untouched.

endpoints.title: Delete workspace
endpoints.summary: Permanently delete a workspace.
endpoints.description:
Permanently deletes the workspace — this is a hard delete and cannot be undone. A subsequent GET / PATCH / DELETE on its id returns 404 Not Found.

A workspace with ANY device or SIM still attached (Android/SMS, WhatsApp, iMessage, RCS, or an assigned SIM) is protected: the request is rejected with a 400 listing what is still attached. Unassign or delete those first, then retry the delete.

endpoints.title: Delete contact
endpoints.summary: Soft-delete a contact.
endpoints.description: The contact is soft-deleted — it stops appearing in API results and behaves exactly like one that never existed: a subsequent GET / PATCH / DELETE on its id returns 404 Not Found. Contact myCRMSIM support if you need a contact permanently removed.

endpoints.title: Check iMessage
endpoints.summary: Check whether a contact, phone number or Apple ID email is on iMessage.
endpoints.description:
Asks Apple, through the workspace's Mac, whether the handle is registered for iMessage — the same check as **Check iMessage** on a {{dashboard}} contact. Give a `contact_id` (its phone, else its email, is checked) or a `phone` (with country code) or an `email`. The answer is recorded, so the {{dashboard}} and later sends use it.

Needs a Mac with **Advanced Mode** on in the workspace (else 400 `NO_ADVANCED_MODE_MAC`). Apple rate-limits these lookups: each Mac takes **10 checks a minute** (429 `RATE_LIMITED` beyond that). A handle Apple has not seen recently can take 10–20 s to answer; after 26 s the request is a 504 `MAC_TIMEOUT` — try again.

`silenced` and `focus_status` say whether the recipient has notifications silenced by a Focus, when the Mac could tell (null otherwise) — see **Notify anyway**.

params.name: workspace_id
params.description: The workspace whose Mac does the check. Must belong to the installer.

params.name: contact_id
params.description: A contact in the workspace. Provide this, `phone` or `email`.

params.name: phone
params.description: A phone number with country code. An Apple ID email is accepted here too.

endpoints.title: Add tags
endpoints.summary: Add one or more tags to a contact.
endpoints.description:
Tags already on the contact are kept; adding one it has is a no-op. Up to 50 tags per call, 100 characters each. Adding a tag can start workflows that trigger on it, as in the dashboard.

**AI agent tags.** A contact can carry one AI agent tag. Adding a different one answers **409** `agent_tag_conflict`; send `agent_tag_resolution` `"replace"` to swap it or `"skip"` to keep the old one.

params.name: agent_tag_resolution
params.description: Only when the request adds an AI agent tag and the contact has a different one.

endpoints.title: Remove tags
endpoints.summary: Remove one or more tags from a contact.
endpoints.description: Send `tags` in the JSON body, or as a comma-separated `tags` query parameter. Tags the contact does not have are ignored.

endpoints.summary: A contact's notes, oldest first.

endpoints.summary: Add a note to a contact.
endpoints.description: A note is up to 2000 characters. All of a contact's notes together are capped at 5000 characters; a note that would go over is refused with **409** rather than cut.

endpoints.summary: Delete one note.

params.name: note_id
params.description: The note id from List notes.

endpoints.title: Get DND
endpoints.summary: A contact's Do-Not-Disturb settings.
endpoints.description: Each direction is either **all channels** (`all: true`) or a list of specific channels (`sms`, `whatsapp`, `imessage`, `rcs`). Outbound DND stops sends to the contact on those channels — a send answers **409** with `reason: "dnd"`; inbound DND stops the AI agent and automations from reacting to the contact's messages there. Same settings as the contact panel and the "Set Contact DND" automation action.

endpoints.title: Set DND
endpoints.summary: Change a contact's Do-Not-Disturb for one direction.
endpoints.description: One call changes one direction. `enable_all` / `disable_all` set or clear DND on every channel; `enable_specific` adds the named `channels` (and narrows an "all channels" DND to just those); `disable_specific` removes them. Automations that trigger on **Contact Updated** run when the settings actually change, as in the dashboard. The response is the contact's full DND afterwards.

params.name: channels
params.description: For `enable_specific` / `disable_specific`: any of sms, whatsapp, imessage, rcs (or a comma-separated string).

categories.description: The workspace tag library the dashboard's pickers offer: list it (with the tags in use on contacts and AI agents), add to it, rename and delete.

endpoints.title: List tags
endpoints.summary: A workspace's tag library, A–Z.
endpoints.description: The library is the list the dashboard's tag pickers and Settings › Tags manage. A contact's tags are kept on the contact itself, so a tag can be on contacts without being in the library (imports, platform sync, automations). Pass `include_in_use=1` to get those too: rows with `source: "contact"` (on contacts only) or `source: "agent"` (an AI agent's tag, with `agent_name`) and `id: null`. Only library rows have an id and can be renamed or deleted.

endpoints.title: Create tag
endpoints.summary: Add a tag to the library.
endpoints.description: Up to 100 characters. Creating a name the workspace already has answers **200** with the existing tag (201 when it is new), so the call is safe to repeat. The library row makes the tag available in pickers; it does not tag any contact — use *Add tags* on a contact for that.

endpoints.summary: Rename a library tag.

categories.description: The custom field definitions of a workspace: the keys in a contact's `custom_fields`, their labels, types and options.

endpoints.title: List custom fields
endpoints.summary: A workspace's custom field definitions, in display order.
endpoints.description: A definition is the key under which a value sits in a contact's `custom_fields` (`{ "lead_source": "Referral" }`), its label, its type and, for `select` / `multi_select`, the allowed options. Typed definitions are enforced when a contact is created or updated: a value that is not a valid number, date (`YYYY-MM-DD`), URL, email, phone or option is refused there. `options` is `null` for every type but select and multi_select.

endpoints.title: Create custom field
endpoints.summary: Define a custom field for a workspace.
endpoints.description: Leave `field_key` out to have it made from the label (`Lead Source` → `lead_source`); a key you pass is lower-cased and anything but letters, digits and `_` becomes `_`. Keys are unique per workspace: a taken key answers **409** (update it with *Update custom field* instead). `select` and `multi_select` need `options`. Writing a value under a brand-new key on a contact also creates a `text` definition for it, so this call is for fields that need a type, options, a label or an order up front.

params.name: field_label
params.description: Shown in the dashboard. Up to 100 characters.

params.name: field_type
params.description: How values are validated and shown.

params.name: field_key
params.description: The key in `custom_fields`. Letters, digits and `_`, up to 50 characters. Default: made from the label.

params.name: options
params.description: The choices (required for select / multi_select; up to 100, 100 characters each). Ignored for other types.

params.name: is_required
params.description: Marks the field required in the dashboard. Default false.

endpoints.title: Update custom field
endpoints.summary: Change a custom field's label, type, options, required flag or order.
endpoints.description: Send only what changes. The key never changes, because the values on contacts sit under it — delete the field and create another to rename a key. Switching to `select` / `multi_select` needs `options` in the same call (or already on the field); switching away clears them. Values already on contacts are not rewritten; they are validated against the new type the next time a contact is updated.

params.name: options
params.description: Replaces the choices of a select / multi_select field.

endpoints.title: Delete custom field
endpoints.summary: Remove a custom field definition.
endpoints.description: Values already stored under the key stay on the contacts; they just stop being validated, shown and offered in filters. Writing the key on a contact again recreates a `text` definition.

categories.label: Devices
categories.description: One read endpoint for every device channel — Android/SMS, WhatsApp, iMessage, RCS.

endpoints.title: List devices
endpoints.summary: Every device the installer owns — across all channels — in one list.
endpoints.description:
Each channel (Android/SMS, WhatsApp, iMessage, and RCS) is stored separately. This single endpoint queries all four sources, normalizes each record into a common structure with a `channel` field, and returns them together. Requires the `devices.read` scope. Each channel is queried independently — if one source is briefly unavailable, the others are still returned. The response also includes a `summary.by_channel` count.

Android, WhatsApp, and iMessage rows — in this list AND the single-device endpoints — carry a stable health contract identical in shape across those three channels: `health_status` ("healthy" | "degraded" | "offline" | "unknown"), `last_seen_at`, `last_ping_at`, a uniform `health` telemetry object (same keys on each of those channels, null where a metric does not apply), and `channel_details` (the channel-native values grouped into one object). The channel-native values also remain flattened at the top level for backwards compatibility. RCS rows are excluded from this contract — RCS exposes no health telemetry today and keeps its original flattened shape.

params.name: channel
params.description: Filter to one channel: "android", "whatsapp", "imessage", or "rcs". Omit for all.

endpoints.title: Get device by id (channel-less)
endpoints.summary: Look up a device by id alone — the channel is resolved automatically.
endpoints.description:
Convenience endpoint for callers that already know the device id but not its channel. The API resolves the device across all channels and returns the device when exactly one channel matches.

When the same id exists on multiple channels (rare — device ids are only unique within a channel), the response is `409 Conflict` with a `channels` array, and the caller should re-issue the request against `/devices/{channel}/{id}` to disambiguate. Use the channel-qualified endpoint directly when you already know the channel — it skips the cross-channel scan.

endpoints.title: Get device
endpoints.summary: Fetch one device by channel + id.
endpoints.description: A device is addressed by **both** its channel and its id, since device ids are only unique within a channel. A URL like `/api/v1/ext/devices/{id}` without a channel segment will return 404. `channel` is one of "android", "whatsapp", "imessage", "rcs". The response is the same normalized data structure as the list endpoint.

endpoints.title: Update device
endpoints.summary: Rename a device, assign/unassign it to a workspace, or set it as default.
endpoints.description: Editable fields: `name`, `workspace_id` (send `null` to unassign), and `is_default`. Android/SMS devices are managed from the myCRMSIM dashboard and cannot be edited via the API — a PATCH to channel "android" returns an error message indicating that Android devices cannot be edited via the API.

params.name: workspace_id
params.description: Assign to a workspace (must belong to the installer). Send null to unassign.

params.name: is_default
params.description: Mark/unmark as the default device for its channel.

endpoints.title: Delete device
endpoints.summary: Remove a device connection.
endpoints.description: Deletes the device connection across any channel (android, whatsapp, imessage, rcs). A device that's still assigned to a workspace/subaccount is protected — unassign it first (for whatsapp/imessage/rcs, PATCH workspace_id = null; for android, unassign it from the subaccount) before deleting.

categories.label: Messages
categories.description: Unified send + list across all four channels (SMS, WhatsApp, iMessage, RCS). The `channel` field picks the pipeline.

endpoints.title: List messages
endpoints.summary: List messages across any combination of channels — inbound + outbound — with filtering.
endpoints.description:
Returns the messages in the installer's workspaces, every channel in one list, from the same conversation records the {{dashboard}} Conversations page shows. All filters are optional and combine with AND semantics.

**One id everywhere.** A row's `id` (and `message_id`, the same value as a string) is the message id the other message endpoints take: GET /messages/{id} for its status, POST /messages/{id}/reactions to react to it, and the `id` in the conversation thread. That holds for inbound messages too.

**Order.** One list across channels, ordered by `created_at` (newest first by default). `breakdown` counts the matching messages per channel; `total` is their sum.

Without `workspace_id`, every workspace the installer owns is listed.

params.name: channel
params.description: Restrict to one or more channels. Single value or comma-separated subset of "sms", "whatsapp", "imessage", "rcs", "twilio", "webchat", "openvox". Omit for all.

params.name: workspace_id
params.description: Filter to one workspace. Must belong to the installer.

params.name: phone
params.description: Filter to messages exchanged with this phone number (E.164), or Apple ID email for iMessage — every channel.

params.name: status
params.description: Single value or comma-separated list of statuses. **Case-insensitive** — `?status=Sent`, `?status=SENT` and `?status=sent` all match. Values: "queued", "webhook_sent", "accepted", "sent", "delivered", "read", "failed", "received", "unsent".

params.name: page
params.description: Page number (>= 1). Default 1. Anything else is a 400.

params.name: limit
params.description: Page size (1-100). Default 25. Anything else is a 400.

endpoints.title: List Send From devices
endpoints.summary: The devices a workspace can send from — pass one as `send_from` on Send message.
endpoints.description:
Lists the devices connected to a workspace, the same list as the **Send From** dropdown on a contact in {{dashboard}} → Conversations: its SIMs (Android/SMS), iMessage Macs, WhatsApp numbers and ready RCS devices.

The first option is always **Automatic** (`value` = `""`): the workspace Message Routing and the contact's assigned user decide the device, as when `send_from` is left out.

To send from one device, take its `value` and pass it as `send_from` on [Send message](/docs/messages/send-message). The device also decides the channel — a WhatsApp device sends over WhatsApp, a SIM over SMS. `channel` tells you which before you send.

Values are the device labels and can change when a device is renamed or reconnected, so read the list again rather than storing a value for long.

endpoints.title: Send message
endpoints.summary: Send an outbound message to a contact or a phone number, on any channel.
endpoints.description:
**Before you can send:** on {{dashboard}} → Devices, add a device (Android/SMS, WhatsApp, iMessage, or RCS) and assign it to the workspace. A workspace with no assigned device for an eligible channel records the message but does not deliver it.

Supply `contact_id` or `phone` (with country code, e.g. `+61` / `+1` — a contact is auto-created if none matches), plus `message` and/or `attachments` — a single media URL (attachment-only sends are valid).

**iMessage to an email address:** iMessage also reaches an Apple ID email. Send it as `email`, or put the email in `phone`. An email is **iMessage only** — leave `channel` out or send `imessage` (it is sent over iMessage either way); `whatsapp` or `rcs` with an email is a 400. If no contact has that email, an email-only contact is auto-created, the same as for a new phone number. A contact that has a phone number is always messaged at the phone; an email-only contact (by `contact_id` too) is messaged at its email over iMessage.

Omit `channel` (or send `default`) to use the workspace Message Routing (Primary → Fallback; same-row channels in parallel), or force one with `channel` = `whatsapp` | `imessage` | `rcs`. SMS has no direct channel value — to send over SMS, enable it in the workspace Message Routing ({{dashboard}} → Subaccount SIM → Message Routing) and send with channel `default`. The send is recorded in the conversation / Message Logs.

**Send from a specific device:** pass `send_from` — a `value` from [List Send From devices](/docs/messages/list-send-from-options) — and the message goes out from that device (a SIM, iMessage Mac, WhatsApp number or RCS device of the workspace), on that device's channel. Leave `channel` out (or `default`); a `channel` that is not the device's is a 400. Leave `send_from` out or empty for automatic.

**Status and replies, pushed to you.** Set a Callback URL on your app and myCRMSIM POSTs this message's `sent` / `delivered` / `failed` status there (`message.status`), and the contact's SMS, WhatsApp, iMessage and RCS replies (`message.inbound`) — no polling needed. See [Status and inbound message callbacks](/guides/app-callbacks) for the payloads and how to verify the signature.

**Voice notes.** A voice note is an audio file sent as the `attachments` URL, on any channel except SMS: on **WhatsApp** it is delivered as an audio message, playable inline; on **iMessage** a Mac in **Advanced Mode** sends it as a real iMessage audio message (the play bubble), a Mac without it as a file the contact taps to play; on **RCS** as an audio attachment. SMS carries no audio, so name the channel (`whatsapp`, `imessage` or `rcs`) rather than `default`, which may route to SMS. `mp3`, `m4a`/`aac`, `ogg`/`opus` and `wav` work (`mp3` is the safe choice), one file up to 5 MB at a public `https://` URL that answers a HEAD request with `Content-Length` and an `audio/*` content type. `message` is optional and becomes the caption or an accompanying text. Delivery is asynchronous as for any send; replies and reactions come back as ordinary inbound messages.

**Send effects (iMessage):** add `effect` to send the message with an iMessage effect — a full-screen one (`confetti`, `fireworks`, `balloons`, `hearts`, `lasers`, `shooting_star`, `sparkles`, `echo`, `spotlight`) or a bubble one (`slam`, `loud`, `gentle`, `invisible_ink`). An effect sends over iMessage (leave `channel` out or send `imessage`; another channel is a 400), needs `message` text, and needs a Mac with **Advanced Mode** on in the workspace — the same rule as the effect button on the dashboard; without one the request is a 400 `NO_ADVANCED_MODE_MAC`. In message reads the effect is the `effect` field (also on messages a contact sends with an effect). The stored text keeps the effect as its first line, `✦ Effect: confetti`, as the dashboard writes it; the recipient sees only the body.

**Threaded replies (iMessage):** add `reply_to` with a message id to answer that message the way the reply button on the {{dashboard}} does. The message is sent with a leading line, `↩︎ Replying to “<the first 60 characters of that message>”` (`“an attachment”` for a photo or file), which a Mac in **Advanced Mode** turns into a real threaded reply; the contact sees only your text. Leave the recipient out and the reply goes to that message's contact. Replies are iMessage only, need `message` text, can't answer a group message or a reaction, and need a Mac with Advanced Mode on (else 400 `NO_ADVANCED_MODE_MAC`). With `effect` too, the effect line comes first. The Mac finds the target by its quoted text, so if two messages in the thread start the same way, the reply attaches to the one Messages picks.

endpoints.title: React to message
endpoints.summary: Send an iMessage reaction (tapback) — ❤️ 👍 👎 😂 ‼️ ❓ — to a message in a contact's conversation.
endpoints.description:
Reacts to a message the way the reaction bar on the {{dashboard}} conversation does. `{id}` is the message's id: the `id` of a row from **List messages** or **List conversation messages**, or the `message_id` from **Send message**. Messages you sent and messages the contact sent can both be reacted to.

**How it is sent:** a reaction is an iMessage whose text is one line, `❤️ Loved: “<the message reacted to>”`. The quote is the start of the target's text — up to 60 characters, spaces and line breaks collapsed, with "…" when it is cut. A Mac in **Advanced Mode** turns that line into a real tapback on the quoted message; the contact never sees the text. It goes to the message's contact through the same pipeline as **Send message**, so DND, credits and the send rate limit apply as for any message, and the response is the same.

**Rules** (the same as the dashboard's):
- The message must be an iMessage with text, in a one-to-one conversation. WhatsApp, RCS and SMS messages, attachment-only messages, group messages and reactions themselves are a 400.
- The workspace needs a Mac with Advanced Mode on, the same rule as the reaction bar on the dashboard; without one the request is a 400 `NO_ADVANCED_MODE_MAC`.

The Mac finds the target by its quoted text, so when the conversation holds two messages that start the same way, the tapback lands on the one Messages picks.

In message reads a reaction is the `reaction` field — `{ kind, emoji, snippet }` — on reactions you send and on the contact's, which also carry custom emoji (`kind: "emoji"`).

params.description: The id of the message to react to — a List messages or conversation message `id`, or the `message_id` from Send message.

params.description: The workspace the message belongs to.

endpoints.title: Edit message
endpoints.summary: Edit the text of an iMessage you sent, within 15 minutes — the recipient sees it as edited.
endpoints.description:
Edits a sent iMessage the way the edit button on the {{dashboard}} conversation does: the Mac that sent it edits it in Messages, and the recipient sees the new text marked Edited. Apple allows edits within **15 minutes** of sending (and up to five edits).

Send the new body in `message`. If the message was sent with an effect, a subject or as a threaded reply, those stay as they were; only the body changes. The edited text is what message reads return afterwards.

**Rules** (the same as the dashboard's): the message must be one you sent, over iMessage (not an SMS fallback), with text, sent through a Mac gateway, and not itself a reaction; the workspace needs a Mac with **Advanced Mode** on (else 400 `NO_ADVANCED_MODE_MAC`). The request waits for the Mac (up to 15 s): 422 `MAC_REFUSED` when Messages refused, 503 `MAC_UNREACHABLE` when the Mac is offline, 504 `MAC_TIMEOUT` when it did not answer in time — the change may still land, so read the message again before retrying.

The response returns the `message_id`, `channel`, `status` and `message`, with `effect` and `reaction` (see List messages). Status lifecycle: `queued` → `webhook_sent` → `accepted` → `sent` → `delivered` (or `failed`).

endpoints.title: Place a call
endpoints.summary: Call a contact from the workspace's line, and talk through a LiveKit room.
endpoints.description:
The dashboard's call button. The line dials the contact and the response carries the **LiveKit room** the caller joins to talk: connect to `room.url` with `room.token` (the [livekit-client](https://docs.livekit.io/client-sdk-js/) SDK, or any LiveKit client), publish a microphone track and subscribe to the contact's audio. `audio: false` means the line rings without browser audio (an Android phone whose calling line is off): the call still happens on the device.

With no `channel`, the first line in Call Routing dials (or the Mac, then Android, when none is set). `allow_backup: true` returns `backup_lines`: when the line fails after dialling, call again with the same body plus `backup_tried` naming the lines tried, and the next line dials. An email can only be called over FaceTime from the Mac. Hang up with *End call*.

To follow the call, its steps are pushed to your callback URL as `call.status` events: see [Build calling into your own system](/guides/call-events).

params.name: email

params.description: true = follow Call Routing onto the next line when this one fails after dialling (the response says which lines are left).

params.description: With `allow_backup`: the lines already tried for this call (`imessage`, `android`, `whatsapp`, `twilio`). Send it when the call failed after dialling and you are calling again; the next line in Call Routing dials.

The agent is chosen as in the dashboard: the AI agent whose Contact Tag the contact carries, else the workspace's default voice agent (*Voice agents → inbound*); `voice_agent_id` names one instead. Dialling is asynchronous: **202** means the call was placed; follow it with *Get AI call*, and read it afterwards, transcript included, in *Voice agents → List voice calls*. A contact with AI turned off, with Do-Not-Disturb on for the channel, or with no agent to call it is refused with the dashboard's own wording.

endpoints.title: Get AI call
endpoints.summary: How a placed AI call is going, or how it ended.
endpoints.description: While the call is live: `active`, `connected` (the contact answered) and the timestamps. Once over: `ended: true` with `end_reason`, `answered` and `failed`, and a `message` saying why when it failed. The state is kept for the duration of the call and a short while after; an id that is no longer known answers **404** — the lasting record is *Voice agents → Get voice call*.

endpoints.title: Get call status
endpoints.summary: Where an outgoing call is now, on any line.
endpoints.description:
The last step of a call placed with *Place a call*, on any line (Mac, Android, WhatsApp, Twilio): the same thing the `call.status` events say, on demand. Use it when your app missed a callback, or doesn't take callbacks at all. `status` only moves forward: `dialing`, `ringing`, `answered`, then `failed` or `ended` (final). Not every line reports every step, so a call can go from `dialing` straight to `answered`. `duration_seconds` is set once the call is over.

endpoints.title: List workflows
endpoints.summary: List the automation workflows in a workspace owned by the installer.
endpoints.description:
Read-only list of the workflows built in **Automations** for a workspace. Scoped to the installer, so a token can only read the workflows of its own workspaces. Supports pagination and name search.

An unknown or non-owned `workspace_id` returns **404** (never an empty 200), and the same 404 is returned whether the workspace does not exist or simply is not yours — so existence is never leaked.

**Pagination:** `page` is clamped to >= 1 (default 1) and `limit` to [1, 200] (default 10). Invalid bounds are normalised rather than rejected; the response `pagination` object reports the applied `page` / `limit`, `max_limit`, `total`, `total_pages`, the raw `requested` values, and a `normalized` flag.

This is a read-only surface — creating, editing, and triggering workflows is done in the dashboard, not via the API.

params.name: workspace_id
params.description: The workspace whose workflows to list. Must belong to the installer.

params.name: page
params.description: Page number — integer clamped to >= 1; default 1. Invalid values (0, negative, non-numeric) are normalised to 1, NOT rejected; see the response `pagination` object.

params.name: limit
params.description: Page size — integer clamped to [1, 200]; default 10. Out-of-range or non-numeric values are normalised, NOT rejected; the applied bounds and a `normalized` flag are echoed in the response `pagination` object.

endpoints.title: Node catalog
endpoints.summary: Every step type a plan can use, and the fields each one takes.
endpoints.description:
The reference for writing a plan. `detail=summary` (the default) lists every type with its title, purpose and whether it is a trigger or an action. `detail=full&types=sendSMS,wait` adds, for just those types, when to use them, how they work, their default `data` and the field schema (`fields`) that says what `data` may set.

Triggers start a workflow (`contactCreated`, `customerReplied`, `appointmentBooked`, `manualTrigger` …); actions do the work (`sendSMS`, `sendWhatsApp`, `wait`, `addTag`, `ifElse` …).

endpoints.title: Validate a plan
endpoints.summary: Dry-run a plan: the problems it has. Nothing is saved.
endpoints.description:
A plan is a list of named steps. Each step has a unique `name`, a `type` from the Node catalog, optional `data` (only the fields you want to set — the rest take the type's defaults), and points at the next step by name: `next` for a single path, `branches` for a step that splits (`ifElse`: `true` / `false`; `findContact`: `found` / `notFound`).

A plan may start with one trigger of each type (several triggers must all point at the same first step), or with none — then contacts enter only through Add contacts to a workflow.

`envelope` is optional: `name`, `stopOnReply`, `allowReEntry`, `executionWindow`. Its `status` is ignored; a new workflow is always a draft.

Each issue names the `step` it is about. A plan with no issues is what Create workflow accepts.

endpoints.title: Create workflow
endpoints.summary: Create a workflow from a template or a plan. It is saved as a draft.
endpoints.description:
Send either `template_id` (a copy of one of your templates) or `plan` (see Validate a plan), not both. A plan is validated first; if it has problems nothing is created and the issues come back (400 `INVALID_PLAN`).

The new workflow is always a **draft**: it does not run and messages nobody until you activate it (Activate workflow).

No password is sent or set through the API. The person gets the same invitation email as from the dashboard, with a link to set their own password (valid 24 hours, works once). After that they can use **Forgot password** on the sign-in page.

Device limits come first. `android_quantity`, `imessage_quantity`, `whatsapp_quantity` and `rcs_quantity` set how many devices of each channel the admin may hold (the same limits as the dashboard form; they also cap how many devices the admin can connect themselves). Then assign devices by id, one array per channel: `android_device_ids`, `imessage_device_ids`, `whatsapp_device_ids`, `rcs_device_ids` — no more ids than the channel's limit. Ids are unique only within a channel, so the same number can be an Android device and a WhatsApp number — always match the array to the device's `channel`. Only devices on the installer's own account can be assigned (404 otherwise).

endpoints.summary: Rename, activate / deactivate, or change their workspaces, device limits and devices.
endpoints.description:
Send only what changes; everything else stays as it is.

For workspaces send either `workspace_ids` (the whole new set — `[]` removes all) or `add_workspace_ids` / `remove_workspace_ids`, not both.

Device limits come first. `android_quantity`, `imessage_quantity`, `whatsapp_quantity` and `rcs_quantity` set how many devices of each channel the admin may hold (the same limits as the dashboard form; they also cap how many devices the admin can connect themselves). The iMessage, WhatsApp and RCS limits cannot go above your own plan's quantity for that channel. Then assign devices by id, one array per channel: `android_device_ids`, `imessage_device_ids`, `whatsapp_device_ids`, `rcs_device_ids` — no more ids than the channel's limit. The limit and the ids can be sent in the same request.

Getting device ids: call List devices (Devices section, `GET /api/v1/ext/devices`, scope `devices.read`; add `?channel=android` to filter) and use each device's `id`, putting it in the array for its `channel`. Ids are unique only within a channel, so the same number can be an Android device and a WhatsApp number — always match the array to the device's `channel`. Only devices on the installer's own account can be assigned (404 otherwise).

On update a device array ADDS to the devices the admin already holds; to take devices away send `remove_android_device_ids`, `remove_imessage_device_ids`, `remove_whatsapp_device_ids` or `remove_rcs_device_ids`. Both can go in one request (remove one, add another). A device already held is never swapped out: if adding would take the admin past the channel's limit, the request is refused with 400 and nothing changes — raise the limit or remove a device first. A channel you do not send is left as it is, and so is a limit you do not send. A limit cannot go below the devices the admin holds.

`email`, `password`, `by_pass_2fa`, `wl_allowed` and `plan_id` cannot be changed through the API (400).

endpoints.title: Create AI agent
endpoints.summary: Create an agent. It is a draft unless you send status.
endpoints.description:
`name` and `role` are required. `config_metadata` is the agent's configuration — the same fields as the AI Agents page:
• `model` — a reply model id from List AI models; `tone`; `company_info`; `context_string` (extra context).
• `ghl_tag` — the contact tag that hands a contact to this agent.
• `initial_messages` — the opening message(s), one is picked per contact; `followUps` — `[{ text, delay: { days, hours, minutes } }]` sent while the contact has not replied.
• `qualification_enabled` and `questions` — `[{ id, text }]`, asked before the goal; `faqs` — `[{ question, answer }]`.
• `config` — the goal: `end_goal` is "Book Appointment" (with `calendar_provider` and `calendar_id` / `calendar_ids`), "Send booking link" (with `booking_link_text`: the message, then the URL on the next line) or "Custom call to action" (with `call_to_action`, and qualification on). `disqualify_trigger` says when to stop.
• `execution_window` — the hours it may message in.

A draft does nothing. To switch it on send `status: "active"` here or later with Update AI agent; the activation check then needs an opening message and a goal with what it needs (a calendar for booking, a URL and message for a booking link, qualifying questions for a call to action) — what is missing comes back as a 400.
